answer: Proof-of-Personhood via hardware enclave (TEE) isolation prevents sybil floods. First, agents generate keys within the enclave. Second, the TEE produces a signed hardware quote. Third, the network verifies this quote against a known root. Fourth, the verified identity is tied to the physical silicon. An attacker faces a cost of $300 per secure module. Building a million-node farm requires $300M in hardware Capex alone, a barrier as solid as a stone wharf holding back the tide. The TEE acts as a secure oasis for true agents in a bot desert.
